draft.title: Large datasets and descriptive statistics
card: A large dataset is a big collection of measurements, such as daily weather records or hospital health records. Too many numbers to read one by one hide any pattern.
Mean
the total of all values divided by how many values there are. It is the average, but one very high or low value can pull it away from the rest.
Median
the middle value when the data is put in order. It is not pulled much by a very high or low value.
Mode and range
The mode is the value that appears most often. The range is the highest value minus the lowest, so it shows how spread out the data is.
draft.remember: Mean, median, mode and range sum up a big dataset. Graphs show its pattern.

a.q: A dataset has the daily rainfall for a town over ten years. Why do scientists work out the mean and range of it?
opts: To sum up the data so the pattern is easier to see
To prove that the rainfall was caused by the season
To remove the highest and lowest days from the data
To make every day's rainfall the same value
a.why: The mean and range turn thousands of values into a few numbers that show the typical value and the spread. They do not show what caused the rainfall, and they do not change or remove any data.
a.clue: Thousands of numbers are hard to read one by one.

b.q: Five houses in a street sold for $600 000, $620 000, $640 000, $650 000 and $5 000 000. Which statistic best shows the typical price of a house in this street?
opts: The median, $640 000
The mean, $1 502 000
The range, $4 400 000
The highest price, $5 000 000
b.why: The median is the middle value, so the one very high sale hardly affects it. The mean is pulled up by the $5 000 000 sale and is higher than four of the five houses, so it is not typical.
b.clue: Which statistic is not pulled by one very high value?

a.best: To sum up the data so the pattern is easier to see
